analysis.one_line_summary: Creator compares tight waves (400° / 8s) versus loose beachy waves (300° / 4s) using the Wavytalk Power Wave.
analysis.full_description: A blonde creator compares two styling techniques on split sides of her hair using the Wavytalk Power Wave deep waver tool. She begins with her hair styled in tight waves on one side and loose beachy waves on the other. She then cuts back to show straight hair, showcases the pink waver tool with digital temperature display, and demonstrates clamping sections at 400°F for 8 seconds for defined waves, noting its blue light negative ion technology. Next, she resets the tool to 300°F for 4 seconds on the other side for softer waves, shows both finished sides side-by-side, and asks viewers which style they prefer.

analysis.transcript_full_original: Tight waves or loose beachy waves? I can't tell which one I like better, and I use the same hair tool for both. It's the Wavytalk Power Wave and it's so good. On the tighter wave side, you use a higher heat setting and a longer timer. I put mine on 400 for 8 seconds, so having it at a higher temperature for a longer time is really going to give you that tight wave. This tool also has blue light with negative ions, so it's going to really add shine to your hair. And on the looser beachy wave side, you use a lower temperature and a lower timer, so I did 300 degrees for 4 seconds. I think the looser beachy waves are my favorite, and I've been wearing this hairstyle almost every day. It's so good for summer. Let me know which one's your favorite.
